title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one named plant is hazardous at collection but useful in a protected mixture
summary: Pliny Natural History 13.43 describes thapsia as harmful even to gatherers, who protect themselves with a wax preparation, while physicians claim medical uses when it is mixed with other ingredients. Preserve reported efficacy and Pliny's disagreement as different speakers. A complete candidate reading of an independently owned admitted nonreserved plant entry would need separate collection hazard, protective application, mixture, recipient, and attributed therapeutic claim while retaining the same plant identity. A generic remedy list, a simple dose reversal, or a single speaker asserting both claims without attribution predicts a different discourse structure. No Voynich plant, word or speaker is independently bound here; this remains a source-led raw idea and no test is selected.

design.mechanism: Source-owned hazard, protective handling, and attributed medicinal-use branches for one named plant
design.unit: Complete Pliny Natural History 13.43 thapsia entry and only a later independently owned admitted manuscript entry
design.contrast: Handling-hazard plus attributed prepared use versus ordinary remedy list, dose-only adverse effect, or one unqualified narrator assertion
design.prediction: A fixed complete reading must preserve who is harmed during gathering, what protects the gatherer, what material is subsequently mixed, and that the favorable medical claim is attributed to physicians while Pliny questions it. Without independently bound participant and attribution spans, the alternatives remain open.
